public_rationale: This sentence passes three sweeping judgments on generative AI as a whole: 'inherently limited, impossibly expensive and economically unviable.' He gives no measure, no scope, and no period. 'Inherently' makes it a claim about the nature of the technology, which a quarter of results cannot settle. The firm-level evidence is also split. Anthropic's S-1, as reported, shows an operating profit of $974 million in Q2 2026, but a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026. Picking one of these as the test would be my framing, not his. The narrower, checkable parts of the same paragraph are graded as separate claims.
limitations: S-1 figures come from news coverage because the SEC page could not be read.

statement.excerpt: No matter how much you dress up whatever AI service has gaslit you into believing it’s sentient, generative AI is inherently limited, impossibly expensive and economically unviable.

from_speaker: No matter how much you dress up whatever AI service
our_interpretation: The sentence makes three sweeping judgments about the nature of generative AI ('inherently'). None comes with a measure, a scope (which services or firms), or a time period.

'Economically unviable' and 'impossibly expensive' have no ordinary test that would settle them for the whole technology at a single date. A single firm's quarterly profit or loss would not settle a claim about what is inherent, and choosing that test would be the evaluator's framing, not his.
The narrower parts of this paragraph (cost and ROI measurability, and whether costs ever fell) are graded as separate claims.
criteria.support_condition: Not adjudicable: no ordinary reading turns 'inherently limited, impossibly expensive and economically unviable' into a test that dated evidence could pass.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not adjudicable for the same reason. Firm-level profits or price cuts would bear on it, but they cannot settle a claim about what is inherent to the technology.
